concept.name: Time stop
concept.definition: An exit rule that closes a position after a predetermined amount of time has elapsed, regardless of price, on the rationale that a setup whose expected move has not occurred within its typical window no longer justifies the capital at risk.
concept.intuition: Good trades usually work promptly; if nothing has happened by the time the edge should have played out, free the capital for a better opportunity.
concept.mechanics: Define a maximum holding period per setup, ideally from backtested MFE-duration statistics (e.g. most winners peak within N bars), and exit at market when time expires if neither target nor stop has been hit. It is usually combined with price-based exits, whichever triggers first.
concept.formula: Exit at t_entry + T_max if no price-based exit has triggered, where T_max is the preset holding limit in minutes, bars, or sessions.
concept.failure_modes: A time stop can systematically cut slow-developing winners just before they move if the window was set from a non-representative sample, and it ignores regime changes that stretch or compress the useful holding period.
concept.misconceptions: A time stop is not a prediction that price will reverse: it is a capital-efficiency rule, and unlike a stop-loss it bounds no loss — loss size must still be limited by a price stop.
concept.example: If 90% of a scalp setup's winners reach their maximum favorable excursion within 5 minutes, the trader exits any such trade still open after 7-8 minutes, win or lose.
